The claim for compensation in the present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) relates to injuries suffered by petitioner in a road accident that took place on 19.05.2017, at about 2 pm, at Copernicus Marg, Madhavrao Scindia Marg, T-Point, infront of Punjab Bhawan, New Delhi, regarding which an FIR bearing no.111/17, under Sections 279/338 IPC was registered at PS Tilak Marg.

The offending vehicle involved in this case is a gypsy bearing registration no. DL-1CM-9920, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no.2.
2.

The case of petitioner, briefly stated, is that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the petitioner was going from India Gate via Copernicus Marg to Barakhamba Road on his motorcycle bearing registration number DL-4SDG- 8651 on the correct side of the road and at normal speed.

When he reached at copernicus Marg, Madhav Rao Scindia Marg, T- Point infront of Punjab Bhawan, New Delhi, all of a sudden, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1CS-9920,
Shailender vs . Shanti Swaroop & on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99110161/
1 which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner and in contravention of traffic rules, came from the side of Mandi House and hit the petitioner with great force due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the petitioner was removed to Dr. RML Hospital where his MLC was prepared.

3. Respondent no. 1 has filed his written statement wherein it is stated that the respondent no. 1 was having a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident which was issued by the Transport Authority, Mayur Vihar (East Zone), Delhi and the same was valid upto 25.04.2019.
It is further stated that the accident took place due to negligence of petitioner himself.
4. Respondent no. 2 had filed written reply wherein it is stated that the offending gypsy is a state vehicle and was on state duty deployment.
It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 was holding a valid driving license at the time of accident.
It is further stated that the criminal case was registered against the respondent no. 1 in which he was arrested and granted bail.

5. On 13.09.2017, the following issues were framed by the Ld. Predecessor of this tribunal as :-
1. Whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 19.05.2017, at about 2 am, at Copernicus Marg, Madhavrao Scindia Marg, T-Point,
infront of Punjab Bhawan, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL- 1CM-9920 being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ?
OPP.
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Relief.
6. The Tribunal heard arguments advanced by Ms. Kanta Choudhary, Ld. Counsel for petitioner and Sh. Neeraj Aggarwal, Ld. Counsel for R-1 and R-2.
The case record has also been perused, including the written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner.
7. The finding on the aforesaid issues is reproduced in succeeding paragraphs hereinafter.

Whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 19.05.2017, at about 2 am, at Copernicus Marg, Madhavrao Scindia Marg, T- Point, infront of Punjab Bhawan, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
DL-1CM-9920 being driven by respondent no. 1 and owned by respondent no. 2 ? OPP.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

In order to prove negligence of respondent no.
1, the petitioner has only examined himself as PW-1 and has filed his evidence by way of affidavit as Shailender vs . Shanti Swaroop & on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99110161/
2 Ex. PW-1/A
wherein
he has narrated the mode and manner of accident and placed reliance upon the attested copy of DAR filed by the IO as Ex. PW1/6.
During cross-examination, PW1 deposed that he was going to his office on 19.05.2017 towards India Gate to Barakhamba Road and the speed of his bike was around 40-50 km/hour.
He further deposed that the offending vehicle was taking turn and he was going straightaway.
He denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to his negligence.
No effective cross examination regarding negligence has been led on behalf of respondents.
8. It can be said that during his cross examination, nothing material could be extracted out from his testimony which can make this tribunal to disbelieve or discard his testimony.
The testimony of petitioner is duly corroborated by the DAR filed by the IO.

Moreover, it has not been disputed that R1 stands already chargesheeted in the above criminal case for offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC for causing injuries on the person of petitioner by his rash and negligent driving of the above said vehicle and the same in itself is a strong circumstance to corroborate the testimony of petitioner on above aspects.
9. Pertinently, Respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.

Therefore,
an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi)
310.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed :-
"......Strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability."

ISSUE NO.2
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
13 . As the issue no.1

has been proved in favour of the petitioner, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
14. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (2011) 1 SCC 343) has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage).
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

sentences.text: The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has tendered on record original discharge summary as Ex. PW1/2 and original medical prescriptions as Ex. PW1/3 (colly).

The discharge summary Ex.
PW1/2 reflects that the petitioner was admitted in Dr. RML Hospital on 19.05.2017 and was discharged on 23.05.2017.
It further reflects that the petitioner had suffered fracture both bone leg right with fracture lateral malleoli left and had also undergone operative procedures.
During cross examination, he admitted that he has not filed any disability certificate issued by any hospital.
Petitioner has also tendered on record original medical bills as Ex. PW1/4 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 4,761/-.
During cross examination, he denied the suggestion that the medical bills filed by him are forged and fabricated.
Needless to say, the respondents has not led any evidence to show that the said bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that he spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he has spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs. 4,761/- towards his medical expenses.
(II) Loss of actual earnings 17.
The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A has claimed that he was doing private work in insurance company and was earning around Rs. 9,000/- per month.
During cross examination, he admitted that he was working with Insurance Company for last about 3 years and was drawing a salary of Rs. 9000/- per month at the time of accident.
In order to prove his employment and salary, he has tendered on record copy of his salary slip as Mark X which reflects that the petitioner was getting salary of Rs. 9000/- per month.
Ld. Counsel for petitioner has filed three written submissions on record which indicate the different income of injured, i.e. Rs. 9000/- per month, Rs. 10,000/- per month and Rs. 15,000/- per month.

However,
the tribunal consider the income of petitioner as Rs. 9000/- per month, which is apparent from the salary slip filed by the petitioner as Mark X. During cross examination, PW1 deposed that after two months of accident, the office had given me two months salary after that the office had not paid me three months salary.
He admitted that he has not mentioned in his affidavit that he has not got three months salary from his office.
Keeping in view the duration of his treatment, this tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 3 months.
Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs. 27,000/- (Rs. 9,000 X 3 months).

(III) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities.
18.
As stated above, the petitioner had suffered injuries in the accident.

However, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries and disability, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Shailender vs . Shanti Swaroop & on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99110161/
5 Rs.20,000/- each is being awarded to him towards mental and physical shock & for pain and sufferings.
Further, an amount of Rs.10,000/- is also awarded to him towards the loss of amenities suffered by him during the said period of his treatment.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
(IV) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 19.
The petitioner in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A is silent with regard to the amount spent towards special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.

Still this tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for petitioner for frequently visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Hence, an amount of Rs.15,000/- each is being awarded to the petitioner towards conveyance and special diet.

Besides the above, an amount of Rs.6,000/ per month for 3 months is also being granted to him towards attendant charges or for the gratuitous services rendered by his family members during the period of hospitalization and immobility.

Therefore, a total amount of Rs. 48,000/ (Rs.
15,000/ + Rs. 15,000/ + Rs. 18,000/) is being awarded to him under this head.

Issue No.3/Relief 20. In view of foregoing discussion, the petitioner is thus awarded a sum of Rs. 1,29,761/-
(Rs.4,761/- + Rs.27,000/- + Rs. 50,000/- + Rs.48,000/-) (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Sixty One only) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR.
However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.
